The other options are incorrect: '1:1:1:1' is the expected ratio for a dihybrid testcross (AaBb x aabb). '3:1' is the expected phenotypic ratio for a monohybrid cross (Aa x Aa). '1:2:1' is the expected genotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross, or the phenotypic ratio in incomplete dominance/codominance.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P1 - Mendelian Genetics
q: What is the expected phenotypic ratio when an individual heterozygous for two traits is crossed with an individual displaying both recessive phenotypes in a two-trait testcross?
explanation: The correct answer is correct because in a two-trait (dihybrid) testcross, an individual heterozygous for both traits (AaBb) is crossed with an individual homozygous recessive for both traits (aabb). The heterozygous parent produces four types of gametes (AB, Ab, aB, ab) in equal frequencies, while the testcross parent produces only one type (ab). This results in offspring with four phenotypes in equal proportions (1:1:1:1). The other options are incorrect: '9:3:3:1' is the ratio for a dihybrid cross between two heterozygotes (AaBb x AaBb). '3:1' is the ratio for a monohybrid cross (Aa x Aa). '1:2:1' is the genotypic ratio for a monohybrid cross.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P1 - Mendelian Genetics
q: Which of the following was NOT a reason Gregor Mendel selected the garden pea (Pisum sativum) for his genetic experiments?
opts: Pea plants are easy to cultivate and have a short generation time.
Peas are normally self-pollinating but can be cross-pollinated by hand.
Pea plants exhibit complex, intermediate blending traits that are difficult to categorize.
True-breeding varieties of pea plants were readily available to him.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because Mendel specifically selected garden peas because they had distinct, clear-cut traits with two contrasting phenotypes (such as tall vs. short, yellow vs. green seeds), rather than complex, intermediate blending traits. The discrete nature of these traits allowed him to easily categorize and mathematically analyze the offspring. The other options are incorrect: 'Pea plants are easy to cultivate and have a short generation time', 'Peas are normally self-pollinating...', and 'True-breeding varieties... were readily available' are all actual reasons why Mendel chose the garden pea, as they made controlled breeding experiments feasible and repeatable.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P1 - Mendelian Genetics
q: If two heterozygous (Ee) individuals are crossed, what is the probability that an offspring will inherit the homozygous dominant (EE) genotype?
explanation: The correct answer is correct because crossing two heterozygotes (Ee x Ee) yields a genotypic ratio of 1 EE : 2 Ee : 1 ee according to a standard Punnett square. Therefore, the probability of inheriting the homozygous dominant (EE) genotype is 1 out of 4, or 25%. The other options are incorrect: '50%' is the probability of inheriting the heterozygous (Ee) genotype. '75%' is the probability of showing the dominant phenotype (EE or Ee). '100%' would only occur if both parents were homozygous dominant (EE x EE).

title: Mendelian Inheritance P1 - Mendelian Genetics
q: Which of the following statement(s) are correct description(s) of Gregor Mendel's life and experimental approach? (Select all that apply)
correct: He formulated the fundamental laws of heredity in the early 1860s.
He carefully gathered and documented mathematical data from his experiments.
He conducted his breeding experiments using the garden pea, Pisum sativum.
opts: He formulated the fundamental laws of heredity in the early 1860s.
He had extensive knowledge of cell structure, mitosis, and meiosis.
He carefully gathered and documented mathematical data from his experiments.
He used a high-powered light microscope to visualize gene loci on chromosomes.
He conducted his breeding experiments using the garden pea, Pisum sativum.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because: (1) Mendel conducted his pea-breeding experiments (Pisum sativum) in his monastery garden and formulated his laws in the early 1860s; and (2) his success was largely due to his rigorous, quantitative approach where he counted and analyzed the mathematical ratios of offspring over multiple generations. The other options are incorrect: 'He had extensive knowledge of cell structure, mitosis, and meiosis' and 'He used a high-powered light microscope to visualize gene loci...' are incorrect because chromatin, chromosomes, and the details of cell division (mitosis/meiosis) were not discovered or understood until decades after Mendel completed his work; he operated purely on macroscopic breeding data.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P1 - Mendelian Genetics
q: According to Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, which of the following statements are correct? (Select all that apply)
correct: Alleles for one trait segregate independently of alleles for other traits.
All possible combinations of alleles can occur in the resulting gametes.
The law applies to genes located on separate chromosomes or far apart on the same chromosome.
opts: Alleles for one trait segregate independently of alleles for other traits.
All possible combinations of alleles can occur in the resulting gametes.
Traits like plant height and seed color always assort together because they are linked.
The law applies to genes located on separate chromosomes or far apart on the same chromosome.
The law only applies to monohybrid crosses.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment states that: (1) during gamete formation, the segregation of alleles for one gene is independent of the segregation of alleles for any other gene; (2) this results in all possible combinations of alleles occurring in the gametes; and (3) physically, this applies to genes that are located on non-homologous (separate) chromosomes, or located very far apart on the same chromosome such that crossing-over occurs frequently between them. The other options are incorrect: 'Traits like plant height and seed color always assort together because they are linked' is incorrect because Mendel studied unlinked traits that assort independently. 'The law only applies to monohybrid crosses' is incorrect because independent assortment describes the inheritance of two or more different traits (dihybrid or multihybrid crosses).

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: Osteogenesis imperfecta and hereditary spherocytosis are examples of autosomal dominant disorders. What are their respective molecular causes?
opts: Osteogenesis imperfecta is caused by a mutation in type I collagen synthesis; hereditary spherocytosis is caused by a mutation in the ankyrin-1 gene.
Osteogenesis imperfecta is caused by a mutation in the dystrophin gene; hereditary spherocytosis is caused by a mutation in the fibrillin-1 gene.
Osteogenesis imperfecta is caused by a mutation in the elastin gene; hereditary spherocytosis is caused by a mutation in the adenosine deaminase gene.
Osteogenesis imperfecta is caused by a mutation in copper-transporting ATPases; hereditary spherocytosis is caused by a mutation in hemoglobin beta chain.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because osteogenesis imperfecta (brittle bone disease) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by a mutation in the genes responsible for synthesizing type I collagen, resulting in weak, easily fractured bones. Hereditary spherocytosis is an autosomal dominant blood disorder caused by a mutation in the ankyrin-1 gene, which codes for a red blood cell membrane protein; this mutation causes red blood cells to become spherical and fragile, leading to their premature destruction. The other options are incorrect: 'dystrophin gene... and fibrillin-1...' is incorrect because dystrophin is mutated in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and fibrillin-1 is mutated in Marfan syndrome. 'elastin gene... and adenosine deaminase...' is incorrect because elastin is deleted in Williams syndrome, and adenosine deaminase is mutated in SCID. 'copper-transporting ATPases... and hemoglobin beta...' is incorrect because copper transporter mutations cause Menkes/Wilson disease, and hemoglobin beta mutations cause sickle-cell anemia or thalassemia.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: Which human genetic disorder is a classic example of incomplete dominance, and how does the phenotype differ between heterozygotes and homozygotes for the mutant allele?
opts: Marfan syndrome; heterozygotes have long fingers while homozygotes have weakened aortas.
Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH); homozygotes suffer childhood heart attacks, while heterozygotes suffer early adulthood heart attacks.
Cystic fibrosis; homozygotes have thick lung mucus, whereas heterozygotes have mild respiratory allergies.
Huntington disease; homozygotes exhibit symptoms at birth, whereas heterozygotes exhibit symptoms only in old age.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because Familial Hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a classic human example of incomplete dominance. Individuals homozygous for the mutant allele lack LDL receptors entirely, leading to extremely high blood cholesterol levels and heart attacks in childhood. Heterozygotes have about half the normal number of LDL receptors, resulting in moderately elevated cholesterol and early adulthood cardiovascular disease, while homozygous normal individuals have a normal count of receptors. The other options are incorrect: 'Marfan syndrome...' is incorrect because Marfan syndrome is inherited in a simple dominant fashion and is a prime example of pleiotropy, not incomplete dominance. 'Cystic fibrosis...' is incorrect because cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive disorder, and heterozygotes are asymptomatic carriers. 'Huntington disease...' is incorrect because Huntington disease is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder where heterozygotes and homozygotes exhibit similar disease progression.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: What gene and chromosome are mutated in Marfan syndrome, which displays pleiotropy by affecting skeleton, heart, and eyes?
opts: The ankyrin-1 gene on Chromosome 8
The fibrillin gene (FBN1) on Chromosome 15
The dystrophin gene on the X chromosome
The elastin gene on Chromosome 7
explanation: The correct answer is correct because Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused by a mutation in the fibrillin-1 (FBN1) gene located on Chromosome 15. This defect affects elastic fibers, causing systemic skeletal, cardiovascular, and ocular symptoms. The other options are incorrect: 'The ankyrin-1 gene on Chromosome 8' is mutated in hereditary spherocytosis. 'The dystrophin gene on the X chromosome' is mutated in muscular dystrophy. 'The elastin gene on Chromosome 7' is deleted in Williams syndrome.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: Morgan's team observed that white eye color in Drosophila appeared only in male offspring, never in females, even though overall inheritance ratios matched autosomal patterns. What explains this result?
opts: White eye color is autosomal dominant; females are protected by a second copy of the autosome.
The Y chromosome carries a dominant red-eye allele that overrides the white-eye allele in males.
Females produce a developmental hormone that suppresses X-linked recessive traits from being expressed.
White eye color is X-linked recessive; males are hemizygous (only one X chromosome) and express whatever allele is present, while females require two copies of the recessive allele to show the trait.
explanation: White eye color in Drosophila is an X-linked recessive trait. Males have only one X chromosome (XY), making them hemizygous — they express whichever allele is on their single X with no second copy to mask it. Females (XX) need two copies of the recessive white-eye allele to express the trait; a single copy is masked by the dominant red-eye allele on the other X. This is why Morgan's team saw only males with white eyes even though overall ratios followed the 3:1 pattern of regular autosomal dominance. The Y chromosome does not carry X-linked genes at all. Option A is incorrect because the white-eye gene is X-linked, not autosomal. Option C is incorrect; no such hormonal mechanism is described in the notes.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: Which X-linked recessive disorder in humans disrupts the movement of copper in and out of cells, leading to phenotypes such as kinky hair, seizures, and low body temperature?
opts: Adrenoleukodystrophy
Menkes syndrome
Muscular dystrophy
Hemophilia
explanation: The correct answer is correct because Menkes syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by a mutation in a gene encoding a copper-transporting ATPase. This defect disrupts the absorption and distribution of copper in the body, leading to symptoms such as kinky, brittle hair, poor muscle tone, seizures, developmental delays, and low body temperature. The other options are incorrect: 'Adrenoleukodystrophy' is an X-linked recessive disorder that affects peroxisomes and fatty acid transport, not copper transport. 'Muscular dystrophy' is caused by a lack of dystrophin, affecting muscle structure. 'Hemophilia' is caused by a deficiency in blood clotting factors.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: What is the cellular defect responsible for the X-linked recessive disorder Adrenoleukodystrophy?
opts: Complete absence of the muscle structural protein dystrophin.
Failure of a carrier protein to transport an enzyme or very long chain fatty acid into peroxisomes.
Deficiency of clotting factor VIII or IX in the blood plasma.
Accumulation of methemoglobin in red blood cells.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because Adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) is an X-linked recessive disorder characterized by the failure of a specific membrane transporter (carrier protein) to move very long chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) or peroxisomal enzymes into the peroxisomes. This leads to the accumulation of VLCFAs in tissues, particularly in the brain and adrenal glands, destroying the myelin sheath. The other options are incorrect: 'Complete absence of the muscle structural protein dystrophin' describes muscular dystrophy. 'Deficiency of clotting factor VIII or IX...' describes hemophilia. 'Accumulation of methemoglobin in red blood cells' describes methemoglobinemia.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: Which of the following are human medical conditions inherited as X-linked recessive disorders? (Select all that apply)
correct: Hemophilia
Muscular dystrophy (wasting away of muscle due to lack of dystrophin)
Color blindness (red- and green-sensitive pigments)
opts: Hemophilia
Muscular dystrophy (wasting away of muscle due to lack of dystrophin)
Color blindness (red- and green-sensitive pigments)
Methemoglobinemia
Osteogenesis imperfecta
explanation: The correct answer is correct because hemophilia, Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy (lack of dystrophin), and red-green color blindness (mutated photopigments) are all classic examples of human X-linked recessive disorders. Males inherit only one X chromosome from their mother, so a single mutant allele on the X chromosome causes the disorder in males. The other options are incorrect: 'Methemoglobinemia' is an autosomal recessive disorder (often caused by a deficiency in NADH methemoglobin reductase). 'Osteogenesis imperfecta' is an autosomal dominant disorder.

title: Mendelian Inheritance P2 - Genetic Disorders
q: Which of the following statements about non-Mendelian inheritance patterns are correct? (Select all that apply)
correct: Codominance occurs when both alleles are fully expressed, such as in IAIB blood type.
Incomplete penetrance occurs when a dominant allele does not always lead to the dominant phenotype, as seen in polydactyly.
Pleiotropy refers to a single mutant gene affecting multiple, seemingly unrelated physical traits.
opts: Codominance occurs when both alleles are fully expressed, such as in IAIB blood type.
Incomplete penetrance occurs when a dominant allele does not always lead to the dominant phenotype, as seen in polydactyly.
Pleiotropy refers to a single mutant gene affecting multiple, seemingly unrelated physical traits.
Polygenic inheritance refers to a single gene that controls multiple different traits in the body.
Multiple allelic traits involve an individual possessing three or more different alleles for a single gene.
explanation: The correct answer is correct because: (1) Codominance is characterized by the full and simultaneous expression of both alleles in the heterozygote (e.g., IAIB blood type shows both A and B antigens); (2) Incomplete penetrance describes a situation where an individual carries a dominant allele but does not display the dominant phenotype (e.g., polydactyly); and (3) Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene mutation has multiple, distinct phenotypic effects throughout the body (e.g., Marfan syndrome). The other options are incorrect: 'Polygenic inheritance refers to a single gene that controls multiple...' is incorrect because polygenic inheritance describes multiple, independent genes collectively influencing a single trait (like skin color or height), which is the opposite of the definition given. 'Multiple allelic traits involve an individual possessing three or more different alleles...' is incorrect because a diploid individual can possess at most two alleles for any given gene, even though the species population as a whole may have three or more alleles.
